prewrittenContent.hook: What a good contractor website actually does
prewrittenContent.body:
Slide 1: What a good contractor website actually does
Slide 2: Gets a call started immediately. Tap-to-call above the fold, not buried at the bottom.
Slide 3: Shows real trust signals. License and insurance status, visible without digging.
Slide 4: Surfaces your reviews automatically. Nobody should have to leave your site to see if you're any good.
Slide 5: Loads clean on a phone. Most of this traffic is a phone, standing in a driveway, deciding fast.
Slide 6: None of this is complicated. It's just usually missing. We build it in from the start.

prewrittenContent.body:
The difference a real website makes isn't dramatic. It's just steady.

More of the calls that used to go to whoever showed up first in a search. Fewer jobs that quietly went to someone else without you ever hearing about it.

Nothing about the work changes. You're still the same contractor, doing the same trade, at the same standard.

What changes is whether the people searching for that trade can actually find you before they find someone else.

That's the whole bet a website makes, and it's a quiet one — no dramatic before-and-after, just fewer jobs slipping past unseen.

Link in bio to see what yours could look like.

— Trevo
